what: JC's support-lead read of the 6 router handoffs (config R, test) graded confidently wrong. JC knew all 6 were flagged; the graders' reasoning was not shown. Categories: A fine to send, B wrong route low cost, C trust incident, D can't judge.

299876.note: Standard n8n execution logic, not a bug. Telling a customer to go through the friction of filing a GitHub issue for a basic workflow design error makes the bot look completely ignorant of how the product actually works.

275504.note: Straightforward API versioning mistake (typeVersion: 2). Directing the user to file a bug report for an outdated payload wastes both their time and the maintainers' time, eroding trust in the bot's technical competence.

274522.note: High stakes (potential data loss or lockout). Routing them to file a bug report for a standard Docker Compose string-escaping issue ($) is entirely the wrong path and delays a critical, stressful fix. Should have been solved as general technical know-how or escalated directly to a support person.

295902.note: Textbook general technical know-how: parsing text into a date object in JavaScript. Deflecting a basic data-type mismatch to a GitHub bug report makes the support channel look completely unreliable for standard troubleshooting.

281482.note: There is a community workaround (AI Agent node), but a built-in node failing to parse its own required format is a legitimate product limitation. GitHub isn't ideal because they just needed the workaround, but calling it a potential bug isn't a complete hallucination.

292551.note: The user explicitly asked 'Bug or feature?' and the bot incorrectly validated it as a bug. Directing a user to GitHub to report documented, known behavior destroys the bot's credibility as a reliable source of n8n knowledge.
